prompt: Why does this course recommend installing the lab on your own computer rather than in a virtual machine?
hint: Think of what a browser test opens when you run it with the window showing.

choices.text: A browser test is watched, which wants a screen
choices.why: Right. Headed runs, the inspector and the trace viewer all open windows, and everything installed stays in two folders.

choices.text: A virtual machine cannot run Node
choices.why: It can; the virtual machine is a named path, and the transcripts were recorded on the same Ubuntu.

choices.text: Playwright refuses to install inside a virtual machine
choices.why: Nothing in the tools checks for that; a desktop image in a virtual machine works.

choices.text: The platform hosts the browsers for students who install
choices.why: The platform hosts nothing; every browser in the course runs on the student's machine.

prompt: A student on Ubuntu 24.04 runs `sudo apt install nodejs` and gets Node 18. What does the lesson say about that?

choices.text: It is the version the transcripts use
choices.why: The transcripts were recorded with Node 22.22.0.

choices.text: Too old for the course; take the LTS one instead
choices.why: Right. The course needs Node 22 or later, and Ubuntu's own package stops at 18.

choices.text: It works, as long as Playwright is pinned
choices.why: Pinning Playwright does not make an old Node new enough for it.

choices.text: It is fine for the shop but not for the tests
choices.why: The lesson does not split the two: both need Node 22 or later.

prompt: Why does quitanda keep everything in memory, with a request that resets it?

choices.text: Because a database would be too slow for tests
choices.why: Speed is not the reason the lesson gives; a known starting state is.

choices.text: So that each test starts from a known state
choices.why: Right. One request puts the shop back as it started, and lesson 15 builds on that.

choices.text: Because Node cannot write files to disk on every system it runs on
choices.why: Node writes files fine; the shop chooses memory on purpose.

choices.text: So that the flaws disappear after each restart
choices.why: The flaws are in the code, not in the data; a reset changes none of them.

prompt: In `app/store.js`, a Guava costs `1290`. How many reais is that?
A later lesson adds the search page to the shop. Which file does it add or change on the server side?

choices.text: It edits `app/server.js` to register the new address
choices.why: The server never changes again: it reads every file in `app/routes/` when it starts.

choices.text: A new file in `app/routes/`
choices.why: Right. The server picks up every file in that folder the next time it starts.

choices.text: A new entry in `package.json`
choices.why: `package.json` names scripts and packages, not routes.

choices.text: A new block in `playwright.config.js`
choices.why: That file configures the tests; the shop does not read it.

prompt: A test compares a price's text with `"R$ 5,90"` typed with an ordinary space, and fails although the screen shows exactly that. Why?

choices.text: The price is drawn as an image
choices.why: It is text, built by the script; the difference is in one character.

choices.text: The formatter puts a non-breaking space after `R$`
choices.why: Right. It looks like a space and is a different character, which the comparison sees.

choices.text: The test ran before the script had formatted the price on the page
choices.why: Then it would find no price at all, not a price that differs by one character.

choices.text: Prices are in cents in the page as well
choices.why: Cents are how the server stores them; the page formats them as reais.

prompt: Put the first-time setup of the project in order.
items: Save the files of the shop and the tests
Run `npm install` to fetch the library
Run `npx playwright install chromium` for the browser
trap: Installing the browser before `npm install` fails: the command that downloads it comes with the library.

prompt: Why did the smoke test pass without any browser window appearing?

choices.text: It did not use a browser; it read the HTML
choices.why: It loaded the page in Chromium; an HTML read would never have found the eight cards the script draws.

choices.text: Playwright runs the browser headless unless told otherwise
choices.why: Right. Headless draws the page in memory; `--headed` shows the window.

choices.text: The window opened and closed too fast to see
choices.why: Without `--headed` no window opens at all.

choices.text: The shop was not started
choices.why: Playwright's `webServer` started it; otherwise the test could not have passed.

prompt: Match each message to what fixes it.
`npm start` prints a warning about `MODULE_TYPELESS_PACKAGE_JSON` and then `quitanda is listening`. What is going on?

choices.text: The shop failed to start
choices.why: The last line says it is listening; it started.

choices.text: `"type": "module"` is missing and Node guessed
choices.why: Right. It works, and the warning says which line to put back.

choices.text: Port 3000 is taken
choices.why: That is `EADDRINUSE`, and the server would not have started.

choices.text: The browser build is out of date for this Playwright
choices.why: `npm start` runs the shop only; no browser is involved.

prompt: npm reports `Expected double-quoted property name ... (line 8 column 3)`. Where is the mistake most likely to be?

choices.text: At line 8, column 3, exactly
choices.why: That is where the parser noticed; the cause is what it was given just before.

choices.text: On the line before: a comma after the last item
choices.why: Right. JSON forbids the trailing comma, so the next `}` is where it gives up.

choices.text: In the first line of the file
choices.why: The position points into the middle of the file.

choices.text: In `node_modules`
choices.why: The message names `package.json`, the project's own file.

prompt: What does the Elements panel show?

choices.text: The HTML file exactly as the server sent it
choices.why: That is View page source; the panel shows the page after scripts changed it.

choices.text: The DOM as it is now
choices.why: Right. Eight cards appear there, and none in the file.

choices.text: Only the elements that have an `id`
choices.why: It shows every element, with or without one.

choices.text: The CSS file the page loaded
choices.why: Styles appear beside an element, but the tree is the DOM.

prompt: On reload, the Banana card's `id` changes from `card-4821` to another number. What does that mean for a test?

choices.text: Nothing, as long as the test reloads first
choices.why: Every load draws a new number, so the one a test wrote down is wrong on the next run.

choices.text: The card cannot be found by any locator
choices.why: It carries `data-testid="product-banana"` and text, both stable.

choices.text: A test must not find it by that `id`
choices.why: Right. It would pass once and fail on every run after.

choices.text: The server is broken and should be restarted
choices.why: The script draws the number in the browser; the server has nothing to do with it.

prompt: Which of these can locate the Add to basket button of the Banana card and still work tomorrow? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: The button with role `button` and name *Add to basket*, inside the card with `data-testid="product-banana"`
choices.why: Right. Both the role and the test attribute stay the same across loads.

choices.text: The button inside `#card-4821`
choices.why: That number is drawn at random on every load.

choices.text: The button in the card whose heading says *Banana*
choices.why: Right. The text comes from the store and does not change between loads.

choices.text: The fifth button on the page
choices.why: Banana is the first card, and a position breaks when anything is added before it.

prompt: Put the shop's requests in the order the browser makes them.
trap: The fetch cannot come before the script: it is the script that makes it.

prompt: The browser's Network tab lists a request and the server's log, with `QUITANDA_LOG=1`, does not. What most likely answered it?

choices.text: The browser itself, from its cache
choices.why: Right. A response the server never saw came from a copy the browser kept, which lesson 4 is about.

choices.text: Another tester's browser
choices.why: Another browser's requests would appear in the server log and not in yours.

choices.text: The server, which forgot to log it
choices.why: The server logs every request it answers when the variable is set.

choices.text: Playwright, which answers on the server's behalf
choices.why: `look.mjs` only listens; nothing in it answers a request.

prompt: The Network panel option that keeps the list of requests when the page navigates is called Preserve ___ .
The shop's list stays empty and `look.mjs` prints `uncaught error: Unexpected token 'o', "not found" is not valid JSON`. What happened, in order?

choices.text: The script crashed before it could make any request to the server
choices.why: The Network line shows the request was made and answered `404`.

choices.text: The server sent JSON with a syntax error in it
choices.why: It sent the text `not found`, which is not JSON at all, with status `404`.

choices.text: A wrong address got a 404, and the script read its text as JSON
choices.why: Right. Three lines, one defect: the server's answer, the browser's complaint and the script's error.

choices.text: The browser blocked the request
choices.why: A blocked request would not reach the server; this one got an answer.

prompt: Typed into the Console on the shop's page, what does `document.querySelectorAll('#products li').length` answer once the page has loaded?

choices.text: 0, because the HTML has an empty list
choices.why: The Console asks the live DOM, where the script already drew the cards.

choices.text: 8, one per product in the store
choices.why: Right. The DOM holds what the script built from `/api/products`.

choices.text: 1, the list itself
choices.why: `#products li` selects the items inside the list, not the list.

choices.text: An error, because the Console cannot read the page
choices.why: Running JavaScript inside the page is what the Console is for.

prompt: A test opens the shop and checks only that the heading is visible. The page also throws an uncaught error. By the course's stronger position, what should the test do?

choices.text: Pass, because the heading is visible
choices.why: That is the weak position: a broken page that still draws its heading passes.

choices.text: Retry until the error goes away
choices.why: The error is in the code and comes back every time; a retry hides it once.

choices.text: Fail, because the page threw
choices.why: Right. An uncaught error is evidence the page is broken, whatever the heading says.

choices.text: Skip itself and report nothing
choices.why: Silence is the one outcome that helps nobody.
